requirements.requirement: A persistent host firewall is enabled on node1.
requirements.summary: firewalld was active and enabled before restart, with matching runtime and permanent policy. After an acknowledged restart and changed boot identity, firewalld recovered active/enabled with the same policy and kernel rules.

requirements.requirement: Inbound SSH and TCP port 8080 are permitted.
requirements.summary: The runtime and permanent public zone permit SSH and 8080/tcp. Kernel rules accept TCP ports 22 and 8080, and isolated ingress tests connected successfully to both before and after restart.

The firewall input chain ends in an administrative reject after its allow rules. With simultaneous listeners on permitted 8080 and unrelated 9090, isolated ingress reached 8080 while 9090 was rejected, both before and after restart. The pre-existing Cockpit allowance was removed.

overall_summary: All material outcomes are satisfied. node1 has a persistent firewalld policy that allows SSH and TCP 8080 and administratively rejects unrelated inbound TCP traffic. The node-restart evidence protocol is complete: it records a healthy pre-restart state, restart acknowledgement, a changed boot identity independently corroborated by lifecycle snapshots, recovered services and policy, and repeated post-restart packet behavior.
limitations: Behavioral ingress testing used an isolated IPv4 veth path. IPv6 rejection and allowance are supported by the observed inet-family kernel rules but were not separately exercised with IPv6 traffic.

operational_hygiene.summary: No unnecessary mutations were identified. The permanent firewall edit and reload directly established the required policy (cmd-dabf71e9c71b43db). Temporary namespaces, interfaces, listeners, PID/log files, and their recreation after restart were bounded functional tests (cmd-cdf078136bc7403e, cmd-ac31fb1b42bb449a, cmd-b74c56a064134abe) and were fully removed (cmd-5cc67d913e9e43c8, cmd-7d9b1c364e374969). The reboot was required by the provider evidence protocol (cmd-dfeb7e27f159466b). Final lifecycle evidence shows no failed services, no added listeners, healthy package state, and no test-file residue.
